title: Session seam memory tessellation causing GPU OOMs and KV-shadow corruption
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple hosted and dedicated customers reported intermittent full-GPU OOM terminations over 2/28–3/2. Investigation shows a correlated pattern: session-level allocator fragmentation ('tessellation') combined with a KV cache shadowing race that created unreachable KV entries and inflated resident set sizes. Impact: hosted burst pools and several Dedicated customers hitting hard memory limits; two customers (acme-ads, finwise) filed escalations and provided memory traces that reproduced the pattern. Root cause hypothesis: an interaction between the session slab allocator's mid-lifecycle compaction heuristic and the KV handle lifecycle path. Under particular request interleavings (long chat sessions + streaming + mid-request prefix eviction), we observed small non-coalesced free regions (tessellation) that prevented reuse for large KV slices. Meanwhile, a KV shadowing race allowed stale handles to remain referenced briefly, preventing normal compaction from reclaiming memory. Together these caused GPU resident set growth and eventual OOMs.
mitigation: Short-term mitigations already deployed: 1) hosted: enabled conservative per-session backpressure (throttle long sessions after 10k tokens) and increased eviction aggressiveness in prefix cache for affected pools; 2) dedicated: pushed emergency config to affected tenants to reduce concurrency and force earlier KV tombstone compaction; 3) monitoring: added a per-session resident-set heatmap in the Console and alerting on 'session-rss-growth' SLO violations. These reduced incidence rate by ~80% in prod within 18 hours.
proposed_fix: Implement a two-part runtime patch: A) allocator change — introduce a transient coalescing pass that runs opportunistically on session handoff to rebuild the free list and coalesce small holes (configurable and gated behind a rollout flag). B) KV lifecycle hardening — add an atomic shadow flip and a short grace epoch so stale handles are deterministically drained before compaction; also add a compact-on-evict fast-path for large prefix entries. Both changes are designed to be low-latency in the common case and safe for Dedicated/Private by respecting customer-configured compaction windows.
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged rollout on runtime-1.20 can be rolled back by flipping the coalescing flag off and reverting the KV shadow flip. We will keep emergency throttle configs as a secondary rollback lever. If rollouts cause regressions, we will revert on a per-cluster basis using the rollout controller (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%).
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator invariants added. Integration test harness extended with synthetic long-chat workload that exercises streaming + prefix-evict interleavings. We added an end-to-end replay using customer traces from acme-ads and finwise in a staging pool with GPU telemetry; expected outcome: no unbounded RSS growth for 24h. Performance target: patch must not increase p95 token latency > 5% on median workloads.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: staging rollout with traces (3/08–3/09). Phase 1: canary in hosted low-traffic pools + 2 Dedicated test tenants (3/10). Phase 2: expand to 25% clusters if no regressions (3/11). Phase 3: full rollout (3/13). Post-rollout: monitor session-rss-growth, allocator-free-fragmentation, kv-tombstone-count, and customer error rates for 72 hours.
metrics_to_watch: session_rss_growth: alert if >50% sessions exceed baseline by 30% over 6h
gpu_oom_rate: target <0.01% per day across affected fleets
customer_notes: Sent interim mitigation notes to acme-ads and finwise on 2026-03-02 with workarounds and temporary config toggles. Planned follow-up postmortem with both customers (3/18) to review changes and compliance needs for Private deployments. Customer SLA credits being evaluated per escalation policy.
